newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's petrochemical output down first 11 mos.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's petrochemical output down first 11 mos.

text.p: Mexico's petrochemical production fell 0.5 percent in the first 11 months of the year compared with the previous year to 1.59 million barrels per day (bpd), state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said Thursday.
The company said from January to November it produced an average 496,000 bpd of gasoline, a 1.4 percent increase from 1995.
Pemex's refining division produced an average 267,200 bpd of diesels in the same period, a 5.4 percent increase from the first 11 months of 1995.
From January to November, Pemex's refineries produced 13.5 percent less kerosenes, including jet fuel, than the previous year for an average 68,700 bpd of kerosenes.

In other petroleum by-products the country produced 416,900 bpd, while in asphalt, solvents, coke, grease and lubricants, output totaled 87,600 bpd on average for the first 11 months of the year, the company said.
Pemex said its liquid petroleum gas output fell 1.8 percent to 250,700 bpd from January to November compared with the year before.
